page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.re8.90xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. The system provides 360 dedicated vCPUs backed by Intel Xeon 8490H processors operating at a base clock speed of 1.9 GHz. It features an extensive total memory allocation of 6144.0 GB, yielding a high ratio of approximately 17.07 GB of RAM per vCPU. Discrete graphics processing units are not present on this instance type.

Network performance is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 96 Gbps, supporting high throughput between cloud infrastructure components. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, meaning persistent storage requirements must be handled entirely through external network-attached block devices. By packaging massive memory density and high vCPU counts into a single host, the server provides substantial computing consolidation for architectures that cannot easily scale horizontally across smaller nodes.

This hardware footprint is suited for enterprise-tier, memory-resident operational demands. Primary target workloads include ultra-large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive distributed caching services, real-time enterprise resource planning deployments, and memory-constrained analytical data pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.re8.90xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 360 dedicated vCPUs from Intel Xeon 8490H processors operating at 1.9 GHz, the instance delivers 6144.0 GB of RAM, translating to an extensive ratio of roughly 17.07 GB of memory per core. The configuration includes no discrete GPUs and provides no integrated local storage, requiring network block storage volumes for persistent file systems. Networking is supported by a baseline network bandwidth of 96 Gbps. Given its massive RAM footprint and dedicated compute allocation, ecs.re8.90xlarge offers substantial resource density for large monolithic architectures, avoiding multi-node serialization overheads. This infrastructure profile is engineered for memory-bound workloads, including large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning installations, comprehensive data caching tiers, and memory-intensive analytics engines.
